1.8 Pushout squares

Using mapping animae, we may dualize the definition of a pullback square of categories:

Definition 1.8.1 (Pushout square). A commutative square of categories

Agda Pushout squares

IsPushout

Definition, checked

IsPushout : {A B C D : CAT}
  {u : MAP A B} {l : MAP A C} {r : MAP B D} {v : MAP C D} →
  Square u l r v → Set (c ⊔ m)
Proof / implementation
IsPushout s = (E : CAT) → IsPullback (mappingOut s E)

Agda The induced square of mapping animae

mappingOut

Definition, checked

mappingOut : {A B C D : CAT}
  {u : MAP A B} {l : MAP A C} {r : MAP B D} {v : MAP C D} →
  Square u l r v → (E : CAT) → Cone (mapPre {D = E} u) (mapPre l) (Map D E)
Proof / implementation
mappingOut {u = u} {l} {r} {v} s E = record
  { left = mapPre r ; right = mapPre v
  ; match = (mapPre-comp l v) ⁻¹ ∙
      (mapPre-cong (Square.commute s) ∙ mapPre-comp u r) }

Remark 1.8.2. We do not assume in the present metatheory that arbitrary pushouts of categories exist. We do not need this as a metatheoretic axiom, although such pushouts exist in all intended models of our theory. We will eventually prove that the synthetic category \(\Cat \) of small synthetic categories admits small colimits, which in particular provides pushouts of small categories.

Proposition 1.8.3. A commutative square of categories

Agda The functor-category criterion for pushouts

pushout→functor-criterion

Derivation, checked

pushout→functor-criterion : {A B C D : CAT}
  {u : MAP A B} {l : MAP A C} {r : MAP B D} {v : MAP C D}
  (s : Square u l r v) → IsPushout s → FunctorCriterion s
Proof / implementation
pushout→functor-criterion s universal E = Preservation.isPullback s
  (Extensions.pushout-extension-property 𝒯 M P s universal) E

functor-criterion→pushout

Derivation, checked

functor-criterion→pushout : {A B C D : CAT}
  {u : MAP A B} {l : MAP A C} {r : MAP B D} {v : MAP C D}
  (s : Square u l r v) → FunctorCriterion s → IsPushout s
Proof / implementation
functor-criterion→pushout s criterion E = Transfer.Detection.isPullback 𝒯 M ℱ P s E
  (Evaluated.map-evaluate s E) (Evaluated.fun-evaluate s E)
  (map-preserves-pullback One (functorOut s E) (criterion E))

About this correspondence

Both implications retain the specified induced-square matching. The forward proof uses uncurrying and transposition of compatible cocones. The reverse proof first applies Map One to the functor-category pullback, then transfers this terminal test to the mapping-out square.

uncurryRestriction

Definition, checked

uncurryRestriction : {X A B C E : CAT} {u : MAP A B} {v : MAP A C} →
  Cone (funPre {D = E} u) (funPre v) X →
  Cocone (productMap (id X) u) (productMap (id X) v) E
Proof / implementation
uncurryRestriction {u = u} {v} s = record
  { left = funUncurry (Cone.left s) ; right = funUncurry (Cone.right s)
  ; match = funPre-uncurry v (Cone.right s) ∙
      (funUncurryIso (Cone.match s) ∙ (funPre-uncurry u (Cone.left s)) ⁻¹) }

outer

  outer = record { commute =

      ((Square.commute right ▷ g₁) ∙ (comp-assoc g₁ g₂ f₃) ⁻¹))) }
